sentences.text: Pehuenchesuchus is an extinct genus of sebecosuchian mesoeucrocodylian named after the Mapuche name for its discovery region.
The animal possessed a narrow, tall lower jaw and lacked the tooth serrations found in other sebecosuchians.
Its largest teeth were the first and fourth, with the first tooth pointing slightly forward.
The type species, P. enderi, was named in honor of the character Ender Wiggin from Orson Scott Card's books.
The preserved lower jaw bone measures approximately 210 mm in length.
The genus was described in 2005 by Alan Turner and Jorge Calvo based on a nearly complete lower jaw bone.
Researchers classified the genus as the most basal (earliest branching) member of the sebecosuchians.
Fossils were found in the Upper Cretaceous Río Neuquén Formation near Rincón de los Sauces in Neuquén, Argentina.
The animal lived during the Santonian stage, between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
